It was played by 12 teams. The national champion was [[Sporting Cristal]].[https://clubsportingcristal.pe/historia/19-historia/campeones/115-campeon-2002 Sporting Cristal campeón 2002][https://depor.com/futbol-peruano/descentralizado/sporting-cristal-vs-atletico-nacional-dia-paulo-autuori-salio-campeon-celestes-fotos-video-95735/ Sporting Cristal: el día que Paulo Autuori salió campeón con los celestes][https://as.com/futbol/2002/12/05/mas_futbol/1039042802_850215.html El Sporting Cristal, campeón de Peru e irá a la Libertadores] == Competition modus == The national championship was divided into two and half-year tournaments, the [[Apertura and Clausura|Torneo Apertura]] and the [[Apertura and Clausura|Torneo Clausura]]. Each was played on a home-and-away [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] basis. The winners of each would play for the national title in a playoff, but a team had to finish in the top 4 in both tournaments to earn the right to play the final. If the same club had won both tournaments, it would have won the national championship automatically. Following-season [[Copa Libertadores]] berths went to each half-year tournament winner, and the best-placed team in the aggregate table. The two bottom teams on the aggregate table were relegated, but a playoff had to be played between the 10th- and 11th-placed teams since both obtained the same number of points (goal difference did not count as a tie-breaker). == Teams == ===Team changes=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
